title: Halfway point reflection — people ops reset
content:
Quick purpose: a compact, messy brain dump to prepare for my upcoming 1:1 with Maya and the quarterly calibration. I want to leave the meeting with a clear priority list (3 things), concrete examples for impact, and the ask I need (time/headcount/mentorship).

Topline message I want to land:
- Focused on stabilizing onboarding + leveling up manager enablement to reduce time-to-ramp and distribution of hiring load.
- Delivered measurable reductions in new hire ramp time (pilot results) and improved manager confidence scores in the enablement survey.
- Need 0.4 FTE for 6 months (program manager contractor) + sponsorship for a manager cohort pilot to scale.

Evidence snippets (short bullets I can read aloud):
- Onboarding pilot: ran 3 cohort intakes in Jan–Feb, N=18, average first-week happiness + net promoter -> +18 pts; time-to-first-prod task down from 32 -> 21 days (sampling, still noisy).
- Manager enablement: ran 4 office-hours, created manager checklist + 6 templates; post-session survey n=22 -> 4.1/5 confidence vs baseline 3.1/5.
- Cross-team wins: partnered with Eng Platform to add a basic new-hire infra checklist in infra repo; reduced incident followups from new hires in first 30 days (ops tickets) by ~30% in pilot org.

Concrete stories to mention (one-liners + follow-up evidence):
1) When we pushed the onboarding checklist to infra repo — immediate drop in follow-up tickets. Slack thread #onboarding-pilot (Dec 21) had the main convo.
2) Manager cohort: Priya ran the first cohort; one manager switched from weekly reactive 1:1s to agenda-driven, showed faster escalations being caught earlier — example: hiring freeze workaround that saved 2 roles.
3) New hire ramp: exemplar — Ahmed on QA team completed first release task in 19 days and contributed a test harness that saved 6h/week for the team.

3 near-term priorities (what I want to get approved or at least aligned on):
- Priority A: Fund 0.4 FTE contract PM (6 months) to operationalize repeatable onboarding cadence + dashboard. Deliverable: onboarding funnel dashboard + playbook.
- Priority B: Launch manager enablement pilot (cohort of 12 managers) with internal mentors and a 6-week syllabus. Deliverable: evaluation rubric + manager confidence delta.
- Priority C: Harden onboarding infra integrations (2 quick wins: repo checklist PRs, infra repo webhook for access provisioning). Deliverable: 2 PRs merged and runbook updated.

Potential risks / anticipated pushback and my quick counters:
- "We don't have headcount" -> propose contractor route, show cost/benefit (estimate: contractor = $30k; expected improvement reduces hire mistakes and time-to-value = intangible but point to reduced incident ops).
- "Not our priority" -> tie to hiring funnel and eng velocity metrics; show pilot correlations.
- "How measure success?" -> propose 4 KPIs: time-to-first-prod-task, new-hire happiness NPS, manager-confidence delta, ops-ticket volume from new hires. Baseline numbers included above.

Open questions I want to ask Maya in the 1:1 (and notes for follow-up):
- Does leadership buy into a short-term contractor to accelerate onboarding? If not, what alternatives (shadow allocation from recruiting/ops)?
- Which stakeholder should be primary sponsor for the manager cohort — Eng L&D or People Ops? (my preference: People Ops + Eng sponsor).
- Is there appetite to pilot in one product org first or cross-functional from day 1? My ask: start with one product org to limit noise.

Tactical next steps (my action items before the 1:1):
- Prepare a 1-pager ROI snapshot (estimate costs, expected delta on time-to-value). Due: 2/18.
- Gather raw survey data and anonymize examples for mgmt readout. Due: 2/20.
- Draft a short pilot syllabus for manager cohort (6 weeks). Due: 2/22.

Scripting for the 1:1 (short, 3-minute pitch):
- 30s problem: new hires take longer to hit productive velocity; managers feel underprepared; this costs time and creates churn.
- 60s what we did: pilot cohorts + checklist + infra PRs; early signals: faster ramp, fewer ops tickets, higher confidence.
- 30s ask: small, time-boxed investment (contractor + cohort pilot) to codify and scale these wins.
- 30s outcome: dashboard + playbook + measurable reduction in ramp and ops toil.

Notes-to-self / phrasing I should avoid:
- Avoid sounding like "more programs" — frame as "fixing a leaky onboarding funnel" and emphasize measurable outcomes.
- Skip long process detail; offer to share playbook after alignment.

What success looks like in 3 months (if funded):
- Dashboard live with baseline + weekly updates.
- Manager cohort completed, confidence delta >= +0.6 (survey).
- Two infra PRs merged and runbook updated.

Longer-term aspirational asks (if above succeeds):
- Headcount request for a permanent Onboarding Manager (1.0 FTE) in next hiring cycle.
- Invest in a lightweight LMS for manager enablement or partner with Eng L&D to scale.

Random scratch ideas (may be noise):
- Slack bot for new hires that pings checklist items and links to docs.
- Pairing rotations for first 2 weeks (optional compensation for mentors?).
- Quarterly "new hire retrospective" with sample of hires in first 90 days to capture friction.

End: keep this doc as my talking points and evidence bank. After 1:1, convert to tidy 1-pager with ROI numbers and update path to shared drive.

Quick refs I want to attach later: raw survey CSV, onboarding ticket logs, sample playbook markdown, infra PR links.
